entries.error: `storage_worker_session_test` "busy native close cannot overtake a held late summary acknowledgement": `eventually` hit its 3 s deadline (~line 351) on `owner != null && owner.sink.records.isNotEmpty`. Passed on Linux. #194 since rewrote the test (waits for the native adapter first, prints setup state on failure, adds a delayed-setup variant). #200 found for a sibling, `native_queue_adapter_test`, that an idle cold native writer need not have drain credits until a bootstrap enqueue is admitted; whether that applies here is untested
entries.next_experiment: 200 runs of the file on macOS with and without coverage; read the owner-state line (and #194's `native_summary_setup_failure` line)
entries.exit_criterion: The loop either names the phase (owner never created vs created with empty records vs later wait) or shows zero failures in 200 runs per mode. Controls: "summary wait evidence separates a missing owner from empty records"

entries.error: `storage_worker_protocol_test` "filesystem fixture writes only validated schema2 and closes before retirement": `classify` returned `retry`, expected `ok` (the test now runs as `contended=false/true` variants since #194)
entries.next_experiment: Run the concurrent loop (four simultaneous copies of the protocol, session and transport suites) on the Linux host against the #194 fixtures; collect the `admission.lock post-failure probe` lines from any exhaustion failure
entries.exit_criterion: The lock holder is named, then a deterministic control reproduces it. Before #194, reproduced locally on macOS only as the symptom: the unmodified base `1d208f31` failed "duplicate manifest fields stay occupied…" once in 60 (`admit` returned null), and with evidence in place later concurrent loops (about 240 runs) showed `admit` returning null with the probe `held` four times, `classify` returning `retry` once (probe `free`) and the post-retirement slot lease unavailable once. On Linux, with an extra 5.5 s control spawning a worker in a parallel isolate of the same VM process, the target test's post-retirement slot-lease assertion failed in 2 of 10 serial runs (second checked attempt observed `held`), against 0 in 50 runs without that control. Hypothesis, not finding: a fork in another suite keeps a closed description alive until exec. Production gap: a non-contention errno is also reported as `retry` (see the known-gap note)
entries.status_note: #194 bounds the fixture on independently checked contention; holder still unidentified, concurrent loops against the #194 fixtures not yet run

entries.error: `model_transport_cancellation_ownership_test` "broken config pipe preserves retry admission after confirmed exit": `TimeoutException` after 5 s where `RpcError` was expected (~line 458)
entries.next_experiment: Require controlled retained-reader refusal and the normal broken-pipe/retry cases to pass on restored Linux, then the final-head restored integration gate; retain original-cause status unless a concurrent replay establishes it
entries.exit_criterion: Close only after a concurrent restored Linux replay identifies the original failure phase and a registered controlling regression fails on a recorded repository commit before the fix and passes on a later recorded commit after the fix, with the five-second retirement bound unchanged. Record the test name and ordered failing/passing commit pair in the closing evidence. The registered "closed fd0 without kernel retirement cannot admit a configuration write" control establishes the fixture admission precondition only; it does not close the original failure. A later hosted run on `cfdbfe6a` reached `stdin-closed` before timing out, so cold launch alone does not explain that recurrence. The Linux fixture now requires kernel `POLLERR` from a write-only pipe descriptor before admitting configuration and retains actual EPIPE, worker-exit and retry assertions.
